cards.explanation: The answer is his son's heart being wise. The writer says, "…if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice." (Proverbs 23:15) Not a fat bank account or a big title, just a wise heart. I think any dad would take that deal, and I would too.

The answer is lips. The writer says, "My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right." (Proverbs 23:16) That's joy way down deep, not a polite clap. Notice what comes right after the wise heart in verse 15: right words coming out of the mouth.

The answer is the fear of the LORD. The writer says, "Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD." (Proverbs 23:17) When your eyes drift over to somebody else's lucky streak, he points them back to the LORD. And he says always, friends, not just on the easy days.

The answer is False. The writer says, "For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off." (Proverbs 23:18) So the writer says the opposite of what the card says. Just before that, he tells his son to always continue in the fear of the LORD.

The answer is True. The writer says, "Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat." (Proverbs 23:20) He's talking about the crowd, not just the cup. I'm a cookie stamper and even I know that two dozen cookies in one sitting never ends well.

The answer is poverty. The writer says, "For the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty…" (Proverbs 23:21) The crowd he warned about in verse 20 is the crowd that poverty is coming for. And he's not done, friends, because drowsiness gets a say too.

The answer is do not despise her when she is old. The writer says, "Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old." (Proverbs 23:22) The word old matters there. Respect for her doesn't expire when her hair turns gray.

The answer is sell. The writer says, "Invest in truth and never sell it…" (Proverbs 23:23) Invest means you put something in and keep it. Truth, wisdom, instruction and understanding are not things to put up for sale.

The answer is the mother who gave him birth. The writer says, "May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice!" (Proverbs 23:25) Verse 24 just before it speaks of a father rejoicing, and here the wish covers both parents. Mom is in it too.

The answer is True. The writer says, "For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulteress is a narrow well." (Proverbs 23:27) I think this part is heavy, so I'll keep it short. The pictures are a pit that's deep and a well that's narrow.

The answer is faithless. The writer says, "Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the faithless among men." (Proverbs 23:28) She's pictured like a robber lying in wait. What grows in number is the faithless among men.

The answer is wine. The writer asks who has woe, sorrow and bloodshot eyes, then answers, "Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed drinks." (Proverbs 23:29-30) The word linger is doing a lot of work there. These are the people who stay put and keep going back for more.

The answer is False. The writer says, "Do not gaze at wine while it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly." (Proverbs 23:31) He lists the red color, the sparkle and the smooth drink, then says don't gaze. So the card gets it backward.

The answer is that it bites like a snake. The writer says, "In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper." (Proverbs 23:32) It goes down smooth, but the end is the snake. A snake bite you don't see coming is the worst kind.

The answer is strange. The writer says, "Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will utter perversities." (Proverbs 23:33) So it's the eyes and the mind that go off track. The writer pairs what he sees with what he says.

The answer is False. The writer says, "You will be like one sleeping on the high seas or lying on the top of a mast…" (Proverbs 23:34) Both of those are unsteady, high or tossing places. Nobody is safe in bed in this picture.

The answer is to search for another drink. The drinker asks, "When can I wake up to search for another drink?" (Proverbs 23:35) I think this one is sad, friends, because he was beaten and didn't know it, and he still asks about another drink. The passage ends on that question.
